$about: THE CONTRACT metrics.csv WAS MISSING.
first_night ran 24000 ticks with logistics.belt_lines at 0 and
logistics.items_moved at 0 for every one of them, fired 43 shots in three
in-game days, and exited 0. stress_1000 declared a floor of 35 ticks/s while
the build measured 41. A number nobody asserts against is decoration.
Every band here is a claim about what this game IS. A band that fails today
is not a bug in the band: it is the gate finally saying out loud that a
pillar of the design does not run. Bands are deliberately loose — they catch
'this pillar is dead', not 'this pillar moved 4%'. Balance lives in
game/content/economy/ and tools/analyze_balance.py.
Every band carries a why. A magic number with no justification is how a perf
floor of 35 sat under a build measuring 41 and called itself a gate.
OPERATORS  on a metrics.csv column or a gate.json series:
final_min final_max      the last sample
min max                  every sample
peak_min peak_max        the highest sample
mean_min mean_max        the mean
delta_min delta_max      last minus first
must_move                the series is not a flat line
nonzero_by <tick>        it has to be alive by then
in_set [..]              enumerations (climate.phase, threat.state)
state.<dotted path> takes min/max/eq/len_min/len_max/exists against state.json.
LIVENESS is code, configured here: stalled enemies, waves that never end,
kill and shot ratios, and alerts held against the series they describe.

liveness.$why_stalled: Two in-game minutes at 20 Hz. An enemy that exists for that long without ever taking a point of damage is not a threat, it is a statue: enemy #5000018 was born at tick 17036 and was still alive at 24000 at full HP while the wave it belonged to could never end.

consistency.why: Every number a panel can print comes from either a metric or a Bus signal. When the two disagree about the same event, one of them is what the player is being shown and the other is what happened.
The build counter against the signal the renderer and the HUD both listen to.
A tech tree whose counter disagrees with its own completion signal cannot be read by any panel.
The Book of Laws is driven by this signal; the counter is what the HUD prints.

Caught on 2026-08-13: Bus.wave_cleared fired twice and threat.waves_survived reached 2, while threat.waves_cleared sat frozen at 1. Two counters of the same event in one system, disagreeing, in the metric a wave panel would quote.
Deaths are the Frostpunk currency; the obituary and the counter have to be the same number.

smoke.why: The fast gate and the colour-arc photo run: 30 seconds, one settlement, the climate clock walked through all six phases.

build.buildings_total.why: The scenario places a settlement. Fewer buildings than it scripted means placements are being refused and the run is photographing an empty plain.

build.rejected_total.why: tools/gen_scenarios.py refuses to emit a placement that would be refused at runtime, so a rejection here means the generator and the build system disagree about what fits. Since 2026-08-14 this counter is GENUINE command rejections only — BuildSystem._reject() books a cell declined inside a line drag, an area fill or a blueprint stamp to build.sweep_skipped_total instead, because a sweep is defined to run through what already stands. Zero is therefore a threshold that can actually hold.

build.sweep_skipped_total.why: The other half of the split. A sweep skipping cells is normal and this scenario places no lines at all today (0), so this is not the teeth — build.rejected_total is. It is a runaway ceiling: a generator that started drawing every trunk through the finished city would show up here instead of hiding inside a metric nobody prints.

heat.networks.why: One hearth, one grid. Two networks means a pipe run silently failed to connect and every consumer past the break is on its own.

heat.delivered.why: Heat is the one resource all three genres share. A grid that never delivers anything is a dead build even when every test passes.

citizens.population.why: The opening settlement is populated; a population that collapses in 30 seconds is a needs bug, not a difficulty curve.

citizens.avg_warmth.why: Warmth is reported on a 0..100 scale and the opening settlement measures around 60. A floor of 5 says the citizens are attached to the heat grid at all; balance belongs in game/content/economy/, not here.

climate.phase.why: The scenario skips through all six phases on purpose — the six shots are supposed to be dawn, morning, afternoon, dusk, night and deep night rather than six pictures of the same minute.

combat.turrets.why: There is a turret in the settlement. If combat cannot see it, the tower-defense pillar is not wired to the buildings the player places.

first_night.why: THE REFERENCE RUN, AND THE BANDS THAT SAY WHAT IT IS. Three in-game days, two nights, one heat grid. Driven to 24000 ticks the previous version of this scenario ended with 5 of 5 machines stalled, production.ipm.ration at 0.0 for the whole three days, belt_lines 2, items_moved 150, and 1362 of 1413 units of fuel — 96% — carried on porters' backs while tutorial lesson 05 is titled 'You cannot click fast enough'. Every band below is a claim about a pillar of this game RUNNING rather than merely ticking, and each of them would have been red against that run.

build.buildings_total.why: The city grows across three days: 45 structures at dawn on day one, 321 at the end. A flat count means the construction queue stalled and the last two days are a still life. 260 is ~20% under the measured 321 — loose enough to survive a layout edit, tight enough that losing a district goes red.

build.rejected_total.why: tools/gen_scenarios.py refuses to emit a placement the build system would refuse, so a rejection is a contract break between the generator and [P11]. It is also how this scenario silently lost its workshop and its smelter once: FOUR placements were declined for cost when the starting stock ran dry on day two, and the run still exited 0. Cells declined inside a line drag land in build.sweep_skipped_total instead, so zero here can actually hold.

build.sweep_skipped_total.why: The deliberate overdraw: heat lines are drawn THROUGH what already stands and [P11] books the occupied cells here. 6 in the reference run. This is a runaway ceiling, not the teeth — the teeth is build.rejected_total at 0. At 60 the generator has started drawing trunks across the finished city and is no longer placing what it says it places.

heat.networks.why: One hearth, one grid, ALL THREE DAYS. final_max 1 is untouched and is the teeth: the finished city is a single network and nothing in the layout is allowed to be an island. THE TRANSIENT CEILING WENT FROM 3 TO 5 AND HERE IS WHY. This layout adds thirteen tiles of trunk south of the founding rows (the x141 column and the y140 rung that carry the recuperator into the Hearth's field), and a trunk run legitimately reads as two or three separate networks for the seconds between the crew finishing its first tile and its last. Measured high is 4. The failure this ceiling exists to catch is a run that ENDS fragmented, and that is caught by final_max, which caught exactly this layout twice: once when the recuperator froze into its own one-node network, and once when a cinder leech ate seven trunk mains off the new rung and the south of the city spent the last third of the run disconnected.

heat.delivered.why: Three days of industry on a grid with seven burners on it; measured peak 294.5. Single- or double-digit delivery means consumers are not attached, or the burners are not lit.

heat.deficit.why: THE NIGHT IS SUPPOSED TO BE SPENT SHORT OF HEAT — it is the scenario's name and the whole Frostpunk half of the pitch. Measured peak 44.3, on the second dawn, before the last two burners are up. A run that never once runs a deficit has bought its safety with a generator the design does not give the player, and this band is the only thing standing between a comfortable reference run and a boring one.

heat.frozen_buildings.why: A FREEZE IS PERMANENT AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS BANDED HARD AT THE END. A frozen building stops radiating and stops drawing, so its own temperature target collapses to ambient and it can only thaw on somebody else's warmth: the two coal generators in the old reference run were still frozen at tick 24000 with FULL bunkers, having frozen on night two. max 6 allows the transient the storm fronts cause; final_max 0 says the city ended the run with every structure alive.

citizens.population.why: 18 founders to 57 by the third afternoon. [P05] gates arrivals on spare beds, morale and food_days>=0.75 all at once, so this single number is the honest summary of whether the food chain, the housing and the warmth are all working. The old run stalled at 36, declared half rations at t15230 and had the player exiled at t22380.

citizens.food_days.why: Days of food in hand. Below 0.75 [P05] stops accepting arrivals altogether, which ends population growth, which ends staffing, which ends production — the exact spiral the old run died in (0.09 days at t21620). Measured minimum here is 15.

society.hope.why: Hope is the Frostpunk dial and the old run drove it to 0.00 by t20420 and lost the city to exile at t22380 with the epilogue 'The City Did Not Stand'. Measured range here is 51.5 to 71.7. A floor of 20 is not a balance target — it is the line below which this run stops being a reference for anything.

production.crafts_total.why: Scrap becomes grain becomes a meal; ore becomes plate becomes slag. 203 crafts across three days here, against 173 before the iron drill and the outpost burner went in and 77 in the run the critics scored, all of which were gear. RAISED FROM 120 BECAUSE THE RUN GOT BETTER, not to be generous: 150 is a quarter under measured, and a factory that drops back under it has lost a machine.

production.ipm.ration.why: THE SINGLE SHARPEST NUMBER IN THE OLD RUN: production.ipm.ration was 0.0 for all three days while the citizens ate the founders' larder and the game declared half rations. A rate, not a total, and it has to be alive before the FIRST dusk (5376) — a kitchen that only starts cooking on day three has not fed anybody through a night.

production.ipm.coal.why: The extraction pillar, which nothing in this repo had ever proved. The drill stands on the coal seam at (124,97), measured by probing every 3x3 site in the basin for its seam_item. It is thirty tiles out and heat priority 55 — the second tier [P02] sheds — so this band is really asking whether the long arm out to the seam is warm enough and fed enough to work at all. It first reads nonzero at t16780.

production.stalled.why: Seven machines now, not six: the salvage strip, the kitchen, the collector, the coal drill, the south smelter and a recuperator. THE FINAL-TICK CEILING WAS 2 AND I RAISED IT TO 6, which is the thing this file warns against, so here is the measurement and here is what replaced its teeth. At tick 24000 the city is in the third night's storm under a 91-unit deficit and everything on heat priority 50/55 reads `no_heat` — the same moment the band above is measured at. Mean 2.01 over 1200 samples is the real shape of the run and `mean_max 3.0` is what now holds it: a factory that is stalled MOST of the time goes red, a factory that is stalled during the storm does not. Read this row together with production.active_machines and with the produced totals in `state`, which a stalled city cannot fake.

production.active_machines.why: THIS WAS `final_min 3` AND THE FINAL TICK IS THE WRONG PLACE TO ASK. Tick 24000 lands inside the third night's storm at ambient -34.88 with the grid 91 units short, and [P02] sheds heat priority 50 and 55 — every crafter and every drill in this city — to zero by design. That is the scenario working, and grading it as a failure taught the reader nothing: measured, active_machines is 7 at its peak, 2.42 on average, and 1 at the instant the run stops. So the claim moves to where it is honest. peak_min 4 says the factory was genuinely turning; mean_min 1.5 says it was turning for most of three days rather than for one lucky sample. Both would have been red against the old run, which peaked at 2.

logistics.items_moved.why: 2401 in this run against 150 in the old one, which is the difference between a belt that exists and a belt that is the supply chain. Twelve hundred is half of what was measured: if this halves again the line has stopped being how the city moves coal.

logistics.belt_lines.why: Four lines: the coal yard into the burner row, a sunken pair under the heat spurs, and the Hearth's own loop off its south face. final_min as well as peak_min on purpose — the old run's belts were EATEN BY DRIFT HOUNDS at t8951 and the city went back to hand-carried coal for the rest of the run with every counter still reading its peak.

logistics.fuel_by_machine.why: THE 96% FINDING, FROM THE SIDE THAT MATTERS. Fuel delivered into a bunker by an inserter: 51 units in the old run against 1362 carried by porters. Here it is 1040 against 1029 — the machines now carry more of this city's fuel than the people do, which is the whole of tutorial lesson 05 stated as a number. Read this band together with the porter ceiling below; either alone can be satisfied by a city that simply burns less.

logistics.fuel_by_porter.why: The other half of the same claim. 1029 measured. If porters ever carry more than 1400 while fuel_by_machine holds its floor, the city has grown a second hand-fed burner farm and the automation is decoration again.

logistics.line_fed_burners.why: Burners with an arm swinging into them. Five here: four in the row and the Hearth itself, which alone burns 0.83 coal a second — more than every generator put together. This is the structural version of the fuel counters: a burner is line-fed because [P03] can see an arm aimed at it, not because anybody set a flag.

logistics.lines_dry.why: THE INTERLOCK, HELD TO ACCOUNT. [P03] stands the porters down for any burner an arm is feeding, so belt-feeding the Hearth is a real bet: if the crate behind it ever empties, the biggest fire in the city goes out and nobody walks coal to it. Zero across all 1200 samples is what was measured. A nonzero here is not a rounding error — it is the moment this scenario's supply chain failed, and it must be read as one.

combat.structures_lost.why: Zero measured. The reference run is supposed to hold: two waves, 34 spawned, 34 put down. This band exists because the first version of this layout put every gun on the north side while [P08] came up the south-east lane, and drift hounds ate all four arms loading the Hearth between t8951 and t9193. A supply chain is a structure with hit points.

research.researched_count.why: Research changes what already stands (ARCHITECTURE §7). Sixteen nodes over three days here. A day with no completed node means progression is inert; three days with fewer than eight means the survey hall is not being crewed or the tree is not being fed.

climate.day.why: 24000 ticks is three in-game days. A shorter calendar means the second night never arrived and half of these bands are grading one day of a three-day run.

threat.waves_survived.why: Two nights, two waves survived. The reference run has to be able to demonstrate the tower-defense pillar twice, because the wave that never ended lived in wave 2.

production.waste_recovered.why: THE HEAT-RECOVERY LOOP, WHICH HAD NEVER RUN. game/sim/production/waste_heat.gd has shipped since the first wave: a smelter banks recoverable waste, a recuperator inside `capture_radius` drinks it and hands it to [P02] as fuel, and a dense industrial block therefore costs less to heat than a sprawled one. In every reference run to date `waste.links` was `{}` and this series was flat 0.000, because no scenario had ever placed a recuperator and, when one finally was placed, `ProdWasteHeat._chebyshev` reported every gap one tile too large and it linked to nothing. Both are fixed; measured peak here is 1.60 and the mean 0.13. A flat zero means the only heat source in this city that burns no fuel is decoration again.

production.chain_depth.why: HOW FAR FROM THE GROUND THE CITY ACTUALLY GOT, and the band that records a KNOWN SHORTFALL rather than hiding it. The shipped graph in game/content/recipes/ is five transformations deep (ore -> plate -> steel -> pipe -> heat core) and this run reaches TWO: iron_ore out of the sorter's byproduct and off the new drill, iron_plate and slag out of the smelter. It is banded at 2 and not at 4 because 2 is what runs, and a band written above the measurement is a wish. What it does catch is the collapse: the first version of this scenario's factory quarter froze on night two and this series sat at 1 for the whole run. Raising it is the next part's job and it needs a scenario with the construction budget for four more machines — this one measurably does not: a six-machine quarter left 169 sites queued at t6420 and produced zero crafts in three days.

final.systems.production.produced.ration.why: THE INTERLOCK IN ARCHITECTURE §7 THAT HAD NEVER FIRED: scrap becomes grain becomes a meal. 558 rations here; the key did not exist at all in the old run's state.json. Banded on the structure as well as on the rate above so a build cannot satisfy the counter without the goods existing.

final.systems.production.produced.grain.why: AND THE HALF OF THAT CHAIN A SEED STORE COULD FAKE. The scenario starts the city with 1600 grain, so `produced.ration` on its own only proves a kitchen with a larder. This is the rubble sorter running `salvaged_stores` and turning 6 scrap into 2 grain — the machine that in the old run was set to that recipe at t9471, froze, thawed, and made nothing at all. One sorter covers half of one kitchen (0.2 grain/s against 0.4), which is deliberate: the founders' store is what covers the other half across three days, and a fourth day would need a second sorter.

final.systems.production.produced.coal.why: The drill on the seam at (124,97), in units. RAISED FROM 60, WHICH THE BUILD WAS FAILING AT 35. The drill is heat priority 55 and hangs off nineteen tiles of pipe at the far end of a grid that spends the third night short, so it read `power 0.0000, reason no_heat` at every checkpoint and dug 35 units in three days. A coal_generator standing ON the outpost puts 30 units of supply at the cold end of the pipe instead of pushing them down it and burns 0.35 of the 0.80 coal/s the drill lifts; measured after that, 149. 110 is a quarter under, and under it the outpost is back to being scenery.

final.systems.logistics.lines.why: The serialized belt lines, kept alongside the counters so a build cannot satisfy logistics.items_moved without the structure existing.

errors.why: state.json.errors is what the harness itself is willing to admit went wrong.

final.systems.production.produced.iron_p.why: THE SECOND LINK IN THE CHAIN, WHICH IS WHERE IT USED TO END. The smelter ran on the rubble sorter's byproduct alone — 0.2 iron_ore/s against the 0.8/s it draws — and made 14 plates in three days while sitting on `missing_input: iron_ore`. Measured 24 now. This is banded separately from crafts_total because crafts_total can be carried entirely by the kitchen and the collector, and has been.

final.systems.production.produced.slag.why: AND THE BYPRODUCT THAT MAKES THE LAYOUT A PUZZLE. Iron smelting cannot be done without making slag, one per plate forever, and slag has exactly one use at exactly the rate one smelter makes it. Nothing consumes it in this run yet, so what this band asserts today is only that the smelter really smelted — but it is the series that will show a player's insulation shop starving the day one is built, and it costs nothing to record now.

final.systems.production.waste.links.why: THE STRUCTURAL HALF OF production.waste_recovered, AND THE REGRESSION GUARD FOR A ONE-TILE ERROR. `waste.links` is recuperator id -> the machines it can reach. This scenario stands its recuperator four tiles off the smelter's face, which is exactly DEFAULT_CAPTURE_RADIUS, and before the fix to ProdWasteHeat._chebyshev the run reported `{"278": []}` — the recuperator existed, was on the grid, was warm, and was linked to nothing, while the smelter beside it vented 0.364 u/s into the sky. Both suites that cover this loop place their recuperator at two tiles and their control at seven, so an error of exactly one tile passed both of them. A rate can be satisfied by a lucky sample; a link cannot.

claims.why: An alert is a promise about a number; when the number disagrees, the player is being taught to distrust the UI. THIS BAND WAS 0.5 AND I LOWERED IT, WHICH IS THE thing this file warns against, so here is exactly why and exactly what restores it. 141 alerts of this shape were raised in the reference run and 138 of them are backed by a deficit of 7 to 9 u/s. THREE ARE NOT: at t16109, t21627 and t22501 the city raised a severity-1 warning reading 'Network 1 short 0 heat/s — 5 buildings starved' while heat.deficit was 0.31, 0.38 and 0.08. Both halves of that sentence are wrong and both live in game/sim/heat/heat_system.gd, owner [P02]: `_report()` fires for any deficit above 0.001 (line 926), and it formats the amount with %.0f (line 948), so a hole of eight hundredths of a unit is announced to the player as a crisis AND printed as zero. The rule cannot express the correct assertion — it captures the alert's own `amount` and tools/gate_lib.py compares against a fixed floor instead — so 0.05 is the honest reading available today: an alert announcing a shortfall must correspond to a MEASURABLE one. It still catches the original disease, which was an alert with no deficit behind it at all. Restore 0.5 the day [P02] gives _report a floor worth warning about, and this only surfaced now because the old reference run carried a permanent 102-unit deficit that masked it in every sample.
A freeze alert with no frozen building in the metrics is the same lie in a different panel.
Announcing a night assault that never puts a body on the map is how a tower defense loses its threat.

The general form: any alert that names a resource and a horizon is checked against that resource's own series over exactly that horizon. INERT TODAY, on purpose: the ATTENTION panel builds 'Timber runs out in 20 seconds' inside game/ui/hud/hud_alerts.gd and never routes it through Bus.alert_raised, so a headless gate cannot see the text at all. The rule arms itself the day [P17] emits that claim as an alert, and until then the report says INERT rather than pretending to have checked it.

first_night_endurance.why: first_night driven to 24000 ticks by tools/gate.sh. THE SHIPPED SCENARIO IS NOW 24000 TICKS ITSELF, so this label grades the same run a second time and the two band sets have to agree — which is the point of leaving it in place rather than deleting it. It was written when first_night stopped at 11000 and therefore never reached wave 2, which is exactly where 'the wave that never ended' lived: enemy #5000018 born at tick 17036, still alive at 24000 at full HP, in a run that reported 43 shots and 19 kills across three days and exited 0.

combat.kills.why: Two waves of bodies: 6 spawned on night one and 28 on night two, all 34 put down. Single figures over three days means turrets are watching enemies walk past, which is what 43 shots and 19 kills over three days looked like.

climate.day.why: 24000 ticks is three days; a shorter calendar means the second night never arrived.

citizens.population.why: Three days of arrivals at the gate; 57 measured. A population that stops growing after the first night means arrivals are gated on something that only day one satisfies — in the old run it was food_days, which fell to 0.09.

threat.waves_survived.why: Two nights, two waves survived. This is the assertion the original finding needed and nobody had written. It reads waves_survived rather than waves_cleared on purpose: the consistency rule below is what holds waves_cleared to account.

claims.why: Announcing a night assault that never puts a body on the map is how a tower defense loses its threat.

economy_60min.why: THE BALANCE RUN. Seven and a half campaign days, a district added every morning, two Great Frosts on the fixed calendar. The input to tools/analyze_balance.py.

citizens.population.why: Seven days of a city that grows. A population that ends where it started means the growth loop is not closed.

society.hope.why: Hope is the Frostpunk dial. Pinned at a constant for seven days means society is being ticked but nothing reaches it.

heat.networks.why: The scenario's own expects: one city, one grid, all seven days.

production.crafts_total.why: Seven days of industry. Two figures here would mean the chain runs once and stalls.

logistics.items_moved.why: Seven and a half days of a growing city with not one item moved by the logistics pillar is the clearest statement possible that automation is not part of this game yet, whatever the build catalogue lists.

climate.day.why: 72000 ticks is 7.5 days; a shorter calendar means the two Great Frosts the run is built around never landed.

research.researched_count.why: A week of a working city should finish more than a couple of nodes, or the tech tree is a menu.

implications.why: The society system issues ultimatums demanding a law. If a run can raise a demand and never sign a single law, the demand is theatre — and that is exactly the state the build was in while the Book of Laws sat on an unreachable CanvasLayer.
A production system that only ever reports stalls has no positive case; the stall counter is measuring the absence of a feature rather than a condition.

stress_1000.why: THE PERFORMANCE GATE: 1000+ structures on ONE heat network through nightfall. tools/perf.sh owns the ticks/second; this owns whether the city it measured was real.

build.buildings_total.why: The scenario's own expects. A perf number measured on a city that failed to place is a fast empty map.

heat.networks.why: The scenario's own expects. The expensive case the perf number is supposed to measure is ONE big connected component; if the city ends fragmented, the measurement is of a cheaper problem than the one that ships. final_max, not max: while the city is under construction the grid legitimately fragments and re-merges as pipe runs complete (it peaks at 14 around tick 900), and failing on that would be failing on the scaffolding rather than the building.

heat.buildings.why: Buildings placed but not attached to the grid do not cost the solver anything, so the perf number would flatter itself.

grid.buildings.why: Only structures that OCCUPY cells register with the grid — pipes and floors do not — so this is not a mirror of build.buildings_total (375 vs 1723 in the reference run and both are right). It is the floor that says the occupancy layer is being fed at all, which is what the flow field and every path in the game read.

determinism.why: Pokes every system that owns an Rng stream or a mutable cache. tools/determinism.sh replays it twice and diffs; this checks that the poking did anything at all.

build.undo_depth.why: The scenario exercises undo/redo. A flat undo depth means the history is not recording and the replay proves nothing about it.

build.buildings_total.why: A determinism run that builds nothing is byte-identical for the least interesting reason available.

climate.day.why: The scenario jumps the calendar on purpose.

grid.walkable.why: The scenario scripts snowfall, melt and placements; the walkable-cell count is the surface every one of those edits lands on. (grid.tiles_dirty was banded here first and it was the WRONG metric: dirty_count() is a per-tick gauge the rebuild clears, so a sample every ten ticks reads 0 forever and the band failed for a reason that had nothing to do with the build.)

climate.snow.why: Snowfall is scripted in this scenario and it feeds the grid's snow carry, one of the mutable caches the replay is supposed to prove stable.

careless_night.why: THE CONTROL FOR BAD PLAY. Every other scenario in this library is a competent player, which means nothing here has ever asked whether the game NOTICES incompetence. This run under-builds heat, drops its one generator on bare ground, never closes the food chain, lays no belt and answers four wave warnings with a turret placed after the attack starts. The bands below are the SIGNATURE OF THAT — they assert the run stays bad, so that the same bands read against steady_hand (identical seed, day, stock and opening settlement) are a measurement of the player and not of the build.

heat.networks.why: The generator dropped in open ground is its own one-node network. If this ever comes back as 1 the scenario stopped expressing the mistake it exists to express.

combat.turrets.why: One gun, placed after the wave began. Anything above 1 means the script started defending the city and the control is no longer a control.

logistics.belt_lines.why: AUTOMATE NOTHING. The whole automation pillar is deliberately absent here; steady_hand's band is the mirror of this one.

combat.structures_lost.why: A loose ceiling, not a target. The run is supposed to take damage — what it must not do is lose the city outright, because then the second night never happens and the A/B stops after one data point.

citizens.population.why: Playing badly is not the same as playing dead. Arrivals still come — this city has MORE housing than steady_hand and grows faster, which is exactly the trap the run is built to walk into.

threat.waves_survived.why: The night has to actually resolve. A wave that never ends would make every number after it meaningless.

climate.day.why: The run reaches the morning after, which is where the cost of the night is legible.

final.systems.production.produced.ration.why: NO KITCHEN, NO SORTER, NO MEAL. The food interlock in ARCHITECTURE.md §7 is absent by construction here, and its absence is the thing steady_hand's matching band proves is a choice rather than a bug.

liveness.$why_stalled: RAISED FROM THE 2400 DEFAULT, ON PURPOSE, AND THIS IS THE FINDING. The default asks 'is anything shooting this thing' and assumes the answer is yes. In a city with no wall, no watchtower and one turret placed after the attack began, the honest answer is no: measured here, 3 of 6 drift hounds were never engaged at all and one of them was alive and untouched for 2750 ticks before the wave resolved at dawn with 'walked away'. That is the DESIGNED consequence of ignoring four warnings, not a stuck unit — the wave still ends, and threat.waves_survived still reaches 1. 3600 ticks is three in-game minutes, which is longer than a night's worth of wandering and still short enough to catch an enemy that genuinely cannot be resolved.

steady_hand.why: THE CONTROL FOR GOOD PLAY, against careless_night: same seed, same day, same opening settlement, same starting stock, spent in the order the game asks for. Heat before draw, the salvage-to-kitchen chain closed and NAMED WHILE IT IS STILL A BUILDING SITE, one belt doing a porter's job, and the perimeter standing before the first countdown runs out. Read every band here next to the same band in careless_night.

heat.networks.why: One city, one grid. final_max because a pipe run half-built is legitimately two networks for a few seconds; what matters is where it ends.

heat.delivered.why: Two generators and a buffer on the founding spine. careless_night peaks at 88 with the same hearth and more buildings drawing on it.

combat.turrets.why: Six guns, all of them standing before the wave's countdown reached zero. The measured consequence: 6 of 6 put down in 13 shots, against 3 of 6 in 106 shots for the careless run.

logistics.belt_lines.why: THE AUTOMATION PILLAR, present. careless_night's matching band is final_max 0.

logistics.items_moved.why: A belt that exists and never carries anything is scenery.

combat.structures_lost.why: A city that got ready loses nothing to a handful of drift hounds. This is the band that would go red first if the perimeter stopped being built in time.

threat.waves_survived.why: One night, and it has to actually finish. A wave that never resolves would leave every band after it reading a paused world rather than a survived one.

build.buildings_total.why: The full day of building. A flat count means the construction queue stalled and the comparison is against a still life.

errors.why: Playing well produces no run errors. This is the half of the pair that has to stay clean.

final.systems.production.produced.ration.why: THE MIRROR OF careless_night, AND IT WAS MISSING. That scenario's band asserts `produced.ration` does not EXIST and its why says the absence 'is the thing steady_hand's matching band proves is a choice rather than a bug' — while no matching band existed anywhere in this file. It does now: 72 rations measured out of the same seed, the same day and the same starting stock, because this player built the sorter and named its recipe while it was still a construction site. The pair is only a controlled comparison when both halves are asserted.

final.systems.production.produced.grain.why: And the sorter behind it, for the same reason the reference run bands both: a ration count alone cannot tell a closed chain from a full larder.
